tasks.title: Slice citations resolve
tasks.summary: sliceSection also takes a heading's name without its trailing parenthetical, and every playbook citation of a sliceable section resolves, pinned by a drift guard.
tasks.objective: Answer closing-review finding f-bs-optimize/integration-aae952a5 (S2): a slice-only bs-wave-runner cannot reach the dispatch.md sections wave.md's steps point at, because `sliceSection` (factory/orchestrator/src/playbookSlice.ts) matches a `##`/`###` heading only by its exact text, the headings carry a trailing parenthetical citation (e.g. `## Round counting and escalation (agent-interviews.md N-4)`), the steps cite short names followed by "above", and step 8 cites a "Dispatch contract" section that no playbook has. (1) `sliceSection`: exact heading match first (unchanged); when nothing matches exactly, match a heading whose text minus one trailing ` (...)` group equals the given name, only when exactly one does; two such headings raise `playbook.ambiguous-section`; the given name is trimmed and its whitespace runs read as one space; `playbook.unknown-section` details gain `sections`, every `##`/`###` heading of that playbook in order. (2) wave.md: every citation in steps 2-10 of a dispatch.md section names dispatch.md and carries its `bs playbook slice dispatch --section "<name>"` command with a name that resolves; step 8's "Dispatch contract" becomes the two sections that hold the lessons and findings splice; step 4's "One message, many dispatches" / "No lockstep barrier" name the common section they live in; "above" only ever points at wave.md text the runner has read. (3) bs-wave-runner.md, outside its SHARED regions: the slice instruction says a section may be named with or without its trailing parenthetical and that an unknown name's error lists the sections; its "dispatch.md's payload contract" pointer becomes the slice command for the section that holds it. (4) A drift guard, test/playbookCitations.test.ts, resolves every quoted section citation in wave.md, dispatch.md and bs-wave-runner.md, and every citation of a wave.md or dispatch.md section from any .claude/skills/bs/*.md or .claude/agents/*.md, through the slice module and, for dispatch sections, the built CLI. Scope decision (planner): the slice verb serves exactly wave.md and dispatch.md and the only slice-only reader is the wave-runner, so the guard covers those two playbooks whole plus every citation into them; self-citations inside run.md or SKILL.md, read whole by the epic session, are not slice-reachable and are not in the guard. Runs after task-14 (bs-wave-runner.md) and task-15 (wave.md) have merged, so the guard is written against the final text of both files. Read factory/specs/active/bs-optimize/epic-spec.md first, including its section "Closing review (plan v5) — changes". TDD: write the named failing test first, watch it fail on the unfixed tree, implement minimally, watch it pass.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-aae952a5 (module half), failing test first in factory/orchestrator/test/playbookSlice.test.ts against the real dispatch.md: `sliceSection(dispatch, 'Round counting and escalation')` returns the section whose first line is `## Round counting and escalation (agent-interviews.md N-4)` (on head dc7db626 it throws `playbook.unknown-section`; the result quotes that failing run). Also: a fixture holding `## A` and `## A (x)` cuts `## A` for `A` (exact wins); a fixture holding `## B (x)` and `### B (y)` raises `playbook.ambiguous-section` for `B` with details naming both full headings; `Round counting\n  and escalation` (a hard-wrapped name) resolves like the one-line name; an unknown name raises `playbook.unknown-section` whose `details.sections` equals the playbook's `##`/`###` headings outside fences, in order (on dc7db626 the details carry only `heading`); a heading inside a fence never matches. Every existing assertion in playbookSlice.test.ts and briefCompose.test.ts is unchanged and passes (a renamed Return discipline heading still fails `playbook.unknown-section`).

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-aae952a5 (wave.md): each citation in steps 2-10 of a dispatch.md section names dispatch.md and carries `bs playbook slice dispatch --section "<name>"` with a name that resolves: step 3 `Fetched and quoted text goes into a prompt fenced, never raw`; steps 6 and 9 `Round counting and escalation`; step 7 `Dispatching the security-reviewer`, `Fingerprint the worktree around every judge`, `Declare each judge's artifact before you dispatch it`; step 8 replaces "Dispatch contract" with `Splice the compiled lessons into every prompt` and `Splice the open findings into every worktree dispatch`. tasks.title: Heavy runs wait in bounded calls
tasks.summary: A new `bs heavy wait` and a rewritten heavy-run fragment let an agent without Monitor run a full suite in the background and wait for it in calls that each end inside the Bash tool's timeout.
tasks.objective: Answer closing-review finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (S2): the shared fragment .claude/fragments/heavy-run.md, stamped by `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs` into the eleven suite-running templates (bs-auditor, bs-coder, bs-grader, bs-merger, bs-reviewer, bs-security-reviewer, bs-spec-reviewer, bs-tester, bs-uiux, bs-verifier, bs-wave-runner), tells agents to run a full suite as a plain foreground `bs heavy run`, whose lock wait defaults to 1 h (heavyLock.ts DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS) while a full suite now takes about 440 s; a foreground Bash call is cut at its tool timeout (120 s unless the call sets `timeout`, 600 s at most); coders and testers hold no Monitor, the diet hook denies a foreground `sleep` of 2 s or more, and a turn that ends with only a background shell hands back. Give every carrier a way to run a full suite and wait for it in which no single foreground call can outlive its tool timeout, the lock is held for the whole run, exit 75 still means `heavy.wait-timeout`, and nothing the diet hook denies is needed. (1) A new read-only verb `bs heavy wait --file <out> [--max-wait-ms <ms>]` (module src/heavyWait.ts, wired in cli.ts and usage.ts) polls `<out>` in-process until its last non-empty line is exactly `EXIT=<n>` and then prints `"done": true`, `exit` and a bounded tail and exits `<n>`; when its bound passes first it prints `"done": false` with the time waited, the current heavy-lock holder (or null) and how long the file has been idle, and exits 124. The bound defaults to 100000 ms, so the call fits the Bash tool's default 120 s timeout as written; up to 570000 ms is accepted for a call whose Bash `timeout` is raised to 600000; anything above is refused. `done`, never the exit code alone, says whether to call again (a suite may itself exit 124). (2) The fragment is rewritten: start the full-suite or e2e command in the background (Bash `run_in_background: true`) as `bs heavy run --label <task-id>-<role> -- <cmd> > <out> 2>&1; printf '\nEXIT=%s\n' "$?" >> <out>`, where `<out>` is the path a foreground `mktemp` printed just before, from a template under `state/results/` (the directory the role's own result goes to, outside the worktree; never `state/artifacts/`, which holds declared evidence) naming the task id and the role, so every run gets a new, empty file with nothing for the agent to remember across runs or re-dispatches; then wait with `bs heavy wait --file <out>` in the foreground, calling it again on `"done": false` without re-running the command, without `sleep`, and without ending the turn while the run is live; pass `--max-wait-ms 540000` only together with a Bash `timeout` of 600000; two calls in a row with `"done": false` and no lock holder mean the run is gone, which the agent reports with the file's tail instead of waiting on. It keeps exit 75 / holder / no blind retry, the three self-locking verbs and the scoped-run exemption. (3) Restamp the eleven carriers with the sync script. (4) Update the pins in playbookOptimize.test.ts and the CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` heavy-run entry. `bs heavy run` itself is unchanged. Read factory/specs/active/bs-optimize/epic-spec.md first, including its section "Closing review (plan v5) — changes" and its subsection "Pre-code review (v6 draft) — changes". TDD: write the named failing test first, watch it fail on the unfixed tree, implement minimally, watch it pass.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (wait module), failing test first in factory/orchestrator/test/heavyWait.test.ts: on a file whose last non-empty line is exactly `EXIT=0` / `EXIT=3` / `EXIT=75` / `EXIT=124` the wait returns done with that code (an `EXIT=124` file is `done: true`, never mistaken for the wait's own bound); a file whose last line only ends in `EXIT=0` after other text (output with no final newline) is not done; an `EXIT=` line followed by more output is not done; on a file with no `EXIT=` line it returns not-done once its bound passes (bound 300 ms in the test, returning within the bound plus 2 s) with `waited_ms`, the heavy-lock holder read from a temporary lock dir (or null) and `idle_ms`; a file still absent at the bound is not-done with `missing: true`. The tail it returns is the last 40 lines before the `EXIT=` line, and when those exceed 8192 bytes only their last 8192 bytes are kept (the cut drops the start, so a failed suite's closing summary survives): on a 50 MB file whose last 40 lines exceed 8192 bytes the module reads only the file's end, and the returned tail is at most 40 lines and 8192 bytes, is a suffix of the text before the `EXIT=` line and ends with that text's last line. The wait starts no child process and calls no shell.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (CLI): `bs heavy wait --file <out>` prints one JSON object and exits `<n>` from the file's final `EXIT=<n>` line (so 75 passes through as `heavy.wait-timeout`), or prints `"done": false` and exits 124 when its bound passes; `--max-wait-ms` defaults to 100000, and a negative, non-integer or above-570000 value is refused with `cli.invalid-flag`; the verb has a usage entry and docCommands passes for every doc that names it.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (each call fits its tool timeout): the test imports the module's default bound and asserts it is at most 110000 ms (inside the Bash tool's default 120000 ms timeout with 10 s for process start), and reads every `bs heavy wait` call the fragment shows: a call without `--max-wait-ms` passes on the default; a call with one passes only when the same sentence names a Bash `timeout` of at most 600000 that is at least the bound plus 30000. A fragment that shows `--max-wait-ms 540000` with no Bash `timeout` beside it fails the test by name.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (end to end), spawned processes under a temporary `BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR` and a temporary HOME: the fragment's start command, read from .claude/fragments/heavy-run.md with its placeholders filled (not restated in the test), launched through `sh -c` as a background child around a node child that waits on a release file: while it runs `bs heavy status` names its label and `bs heavy wait --max-wait-ms 300` exits 124 with `"done": false`; after the release `bs heavy wait` exits with the node child's code, the out file's last line is `EXIT=<n>` on its own line even though the child printed no final newline, and `bs heavy status` prints `{}` (the lock was held for the whole run, then released). With the lock pre-held by a live pid and `--max-wait-ms 200` added to the start command's `bs heavy run`, the out file ends `EXIT=75` and `bs heavy wait` exits 75 with the holder's pid and label in its output. A start whose shell is killed before it writes `EXIT=` gives two `bs heavy wait` calls in a row with `"done": false` and `holder` null. The fragment's `mktemp` step, read from the fragment with its placeholders filled, run twice under a temporary `state/results/` prints two distinct paths to existing empty files, and `bs heavy wait --max-wait-ms 300` on a fresh one is not done. Every child is killed or awaited in `afterEach`.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (fragment): .claude/fragments/heavy-run.md states the background start (`run_in_background: true`, the start command above with the exit code written by `printf` on a line of its own), how `<out>` is made (a foreground `mktemp` from a template under `state/results/` naming the task id and the role, run before every start; not `state/artifacts/`), the foreground `bs heavy wait --file <out>` and the Bash `timeout` that goes with a longer `--max-wait-ms`, that `"done"` and not the exit code decides whether to call again and that the agent calls again without re-running the command or using `sleep` and does not end its turn while the run is live, the stop rule (two `"done": false` in a row with no lock holder: the run is gone, report it with the tail), exit 75 = `heavy.wait-timeout` with the holder put in the result and no blind retry, the `bs gate run` / `bs integration check` / `bs queue run` exclusion and the scoped-run exemption. playbookOptimize.test.ts's fragment pins are replaced by pins of each of these, none weaker than the one it replaces, and its other assertions are unchanged; the eleven-carrier and no-restatement tests pass (no template names `bs heavy run` or `bs heavy wait` outside the region).

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (nothing the hooks deny): `dietDecision` returns no deny for the fragment's `mktemp` step and wait command in the foreground and for its start command with `run_in_background: true`; `decideHookPayload` allows all three for an unleased session and under a judge lease for each of the six judge roles (a temporary lease dir built the way hookDecision's lease tests build one), with `<out>` where the fragment says. If no `<out>` location satisfies the judge sandbox without editing guardrails.yml or policy.ts, the task stops and reports; it never widens the sandbox.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-dcc5330f (stamps and changelog): `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs` restamps exactly the eleven carriers and `--check` then reports 0 drifted; templateFragments.test.ts passes unchanged; the CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` heavy-run entry states the background start and `bs heavy wait`, and the CHANGELOG feature test passes.

Gate, run from the worktree root on the task's own tree and each output read to its end: `pnpm run test` (the full root suite, never a scoped vitest run), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm biome check .`, `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs --check`. The role templates the harness loads predate the heavy-run fix, so the full suite runs as the wave brief directs (epic spec, "Pre-code review (v6 draft) — changes", item 6): a background task under the heavy lock writing a fresh output file outside the worktree whose last line is `EXIT=<n>` on a line of its own, waited for in foreground calls that each end inside the Bash tool's timeout and use no `sleep`; the result quotes that file's final summary lines and its `EXIT=0`. All five green before hand-back.

functional_clauses: `bs heavy run` keeps its flags, its default lock wait (heavyLock.ts DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MS, 1 h) and its exit codes; the `bs heavy run` process holds the lock for the whole child run, so a background start keeps the machine serialized exactly as a foreground one.
`bs heavy wait` takes no lock, writes nothing, spawns nothing and runs no shell; it polls in-process at most every 2000 ms and reads only the file's end.

`bs heavy wait` output: `"done": true` with `exit` and a tail of the last 40 lines before the `EXIT=` line, of which at most the last 8192 bytes are kept, exiting `<n>` from the file's final `EXIT=<n>` line; or `"done": false` with `waited_ms`, `holder` and `idle_ms` (or `missing: true`), exiting 124. `done` is the signal; the exit code alone is not.

Its bound defaults to 100000 ms, which fits the Bash tool's default 120 s timeout as written; values up to 570000 ms are accepted and the fragment shows them only beside a Bash `timeout` of 600000; above 570000 is refused.

The fragment's start command writes the exit code with `printf` on a line of its own, so a suite whose output lacks a final newline still ends the file with an `EXIT=<n>` line; `<out>` is minted by a foreground `mktemp` before every start, from a template under `state/results/` naming the task id and role, so it is new and empty for every run with no counter for the agent to keep; it lies outside the worktree and outside `state/artifacts/`.

The fragment stays the rule's one home (epic D9): brief compose, wave.md and dispatch.md gain no copy. Agent templates change only inside their `heavy-run` SHARED region, written by `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs`, never by hand.
guardrails.yml and policy.ts are not edited; the sandbox is never widened to make the documented commands pass.

Open source: no other project's name in code, tests, fixtures or docs; use `project-a` / `<project>`.
Stay inside this task's claims; every other file is read-only, including factory/specs/** (the epic spec is the planner's).
Tests that spawn processes clean up every child they start (killed or awaited in an `afterEach`/`finally`) and never signal a pid they did not start.
Tests that take a lock point it at a temporary directory (`BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR` or the `lockDir` option), never the machine's real locks under `~/.blacksmith/locks`.
The fragment is stamped into eleven system prompts: keep it to one short block holding the two commands and the rules above.
Usage entry and `--max-wait-ms` validation reuse the CLI's existing flag helpers (`boundedIntFlag`).

tasks.title: Every landing tested on its own head
tasks.summary: The merge queue's `step` holds the heavy lock from rebase through merge and lands only on the head its suite ran on; run.md says the epic session admits after every landing, a dispatched runner's included.
tasks.objective: Answer closing-review finding f-bs-optimize/integration-a2f0a33f (S2): with rolling admission two `bs queue run` for one epic can overlap, and queue.ts `step` rebases at `certifyAndRebase`, then waits for the heavy lock and runs the cumulative suite, then merges with `--no-ff` (or `mergeWithoutWorktree`, which re-reads the head) without re-checking the integration head, so a task can land onto a head its suite never ran against; run.md also says "one wave at a time" (line 6) against epic D6 and its own rolling-admission paragraph. Rolling admission stays (operator decision). (1) `step` takes the heavy lock once, before certify-and-rebase, and holds it through the merge and the `wave-merged` append; its suite runs under that same hold with `heavyChildEnv(process.env, lease)`, never a second acquire; so queue steps, of one epic or several, never interleave between a rebase and its merge. (2) `step` lands only onto the integration head the task was rebased onto and tested on (compare-and-swap): otherwise it reports `integration-moved`, logs a blocked `execution.env-failure` naming both heads and lands nothing, as the batch path already does. The batch path keeps its compare-and-swap landing and its per-suite lock. (3) run.md: drop "one wave at a time"; say waves overlap under rolling admission and that the epic session is the only session that admits, right after each landing in every shape (item 6 below). wave.md step 10: `bs queue run` holds the heavy lock per task from rebase through merge, so queue runs of one epic take turns and each suite runs on the head it lands on; `integration-moved` means a writer outside the queue moved the branch, nothing landed, re-run `bs queue run` for those tasks; and, in plain words for its slice-only reader, that admitting the wave's own passed tasks into the merge queue (`bs queue run`) is the runner's job and admitting tasks to work (`bs wave next`, `bs wave check`) is the epic session's, so the runner never runs `bs wave next` to admit. Step 10's existing "before admitting", "keep going to admission" and "Then admit into the merge queue" (wave.md:372, :385, :395) stay merge-queue admission and are qualified as such wherever they could be read as admitting work. (4) Git subprocesses `step` starts while it holds the lock (the rebase and the `--no-ff` merge, which run the project's git hooks) get `heavyChildEnv(process.env, lease)` like the suite child (the parent env minus every `BS_`/`SMITH_` variable, plus `BS_HEAVY_LOCK_TOKEN` and `BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR`), so a hook that calls `bs heavy run` re-enters instead of waiting on its own parent. (5) A head that moved wins over a conflict: when the integration head differs from the one the suite ran on, `step` returns `integration-moved` without attempting the merge, whether or not the task would also conflict with the new head (the next `bs queue run` rebases and reports `rebase-conflict` if it does); queue.test.ts's 'throws on a tree-less merge conflict and leaves the integration ref alone' is replaced accordingly. (6) Rolling admission for a dispatched runner (operator decision: after every merge, any ready non-overlapping task is admitted at once): the epic session dispatches a `bs-wave-runner` as a background agent (`run_in_background: true`) and watches `bs event tail <session-id> --lineage --follow` with the Monitor tool; on each `wave-merged` it runs `bs wave next` and admits what it returns at once, as a wave of its own (inline or another runner); a runner never admits tasks to work (it only queues its own passed tasks with `bs queue run`); when the Agent call cannot run in the background, the epic session runs the wave inline or in a session it drives itself rather than block on a runner. (7) Test the interleaving. task-13 edits wave.md after this task merges, so keep the edits to step 10 (and the merge-queue paragraph of "Run the whole wave at once" if it needs a word), and cite no section of another playbook by quoted name. Read factory/specs/active/bs-optimize/epic-spec.md first, including its section "Closing review (plan v5) — changes" and its subsection "Pre-code review (v6 draft) — changes". TDD: write the named failing test first, watch it fail on the unfixed tree, implement minimally, watch it pass.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-a2f0a33f (interleaving), failing test first in factory/orchestrator/test/queueSerial.test.ts: on a temporary repo and a temporary lock dir pre-held by a test-owned record (`isPidAlive` injected), two `step` calls of one epic start concurrently: task B changes `api.txt`, task C (claim-disjoint) changes `use.txt` to rely on the old `api.txt`; the test command fails on a tree holding both changes and appends the tree it ran on (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) to a log outside the repo. The test releases its record only after both steps have probed the held lock (counted through the injected `isPidAlive`; no timing sleeps). With the fix, exactly one of B and C is `merged` and the other `tests-failed`, and after every landing the integration branch's tree appears in the tested-tree log. On head dc7db626 the same test fails because both are `merged` and the final integration tree is absent from the log; the result quotes that failing run.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-a2f0a33f (head moved by an outside writer), in queueSerial.test.ts: while `step`'s suite runs, its test command moves `bs/<epic>/integration` (a commit no queue made); `step` returns `integration-moved` without attempting the merge, the integration head is the outside commit (the task did not land), and the events sink holds a blocked `execution.env-failure` event naming both heads and no `wave-merged` for the task. Covered once with no worktree holding the integration branch (the outside writer moves the ref with `git update-ref`) and once with a clean holder worktree (the outside writer commits in that worktree, so it stays clean and the `integration-dirty` refusal does not fire first). A moved head wins over a conflict: when the outside commit also conflicts with the task, `step` still returns `integration-moved` and throws nothing, and a second `step` on the same task then reports `rebase-conflict` naming the file. A second `step` after a non-conflicting move rebases onto the moved head, re-runs the suite and merges.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-a2f0a33f (batch path): a `step` landing between a batch candidate's build and its land leaves every task of the batch `integration-moved` with nothing of the batch landed; the existing `integration-moved` batch test passes unchanged.

tasks.title: Sleep operands read as sleep reads them
tasks.summary: The diet hook reads exponent, hex and signed `sleep` operands as their real duration, and counts an operand it cannot read as unknown length.
tasks.objective: Answer closing-review finding f-bs-optimize/integration-1e75d554 (S4): hookDecision.ts `sleepDuration` reads only operands matching `NUMBER_RE` (plain decimals) and treats every other operand as "sleep rejects it at once", so `sleep 1e3` and `sleep 0x10` pass the decision-15 deny although macOS and GNU `sleep` both block on them. Read each operand the way strtod reads one (optional leading `+`; decimal with optional fraction and exponent; `0x` hex with optional fraction and binary exponent; `inf`/`infinity` in any case), greedily, then at most one of `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`; an operand that reader cannot read counts as unknown length (2 s or more, epic D4's duration rule), not as an instant error. `sleep` with no operand stays allowed. Only the operand reader changes: the shell scanner, the wrappers, the failure rule and the deny reason format stay as they are. policy.ts's `PREFIX_OPERAND_RE` reads prefix-word durations the same plain-decimal way, but the planner's probe on dc7db626 found every guard rule still denying behind `timeout 1e1` / `timeout 0x10`, so it is out of this task. Read factory/specs/active/bs-optimize/epic-spec.md first, including its section "Closing review (plan v5) — changes". TDD: write the named failing test first, watch it fail on the unfixed tree, implement minimally, watch it pass.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-1e75d554 (deny rows), failing test first in factory/orchestrator/test/hookDecision.test.ts, one test per row through `dietDecision` on a Bash payload with `run_in_background` unset, each reason naming the duration: `sleep 1e3` (1000 s), `sleep 0x10` (16 s), `sleep 2e0` (2 s), `sleep 2E0` (2 s), `sleep +5` (5 s), `sleep 1e1m` (600 s), `sleep 5e-1m` (30 s), `sleep 0x1d` (29 s: the hex digit `d` belongs to the number, as strtod reads it), `sleep 1 0x1` (2 s), `sleep 5.` (5 s), `sleep .5e1` (5 s), `timeout 30 sleep 1e3` (1000 s). On head dc7db626 each row except `sleep 5.` (which the old reader already read) returns no deny (`findForegroundSleeps` returns []); the result quotes that failing run.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-1e75d554 (allow rows): `sleep 1e0`, `sleep 0x1`, `sleep 5e-1`, `sleep 1e-3`, `sleep 0x1p0`, `sleep .5`, `sleep 1.` (each under 2 s), `sleep 1e3 &`, `sleep 1e3` with `run_in_background: true`, and `timeout 1e3 pnpm test` (`timeout`'s own duration is not a sleep) get no diet deny.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-1e75d554 (unknown length): `sleep abc`, `sleep 1x`, `sleep nan`, `sleep .` and `sleep 1,5` are denied as unknown length (the reason says `unknown`), where dc7db626 allowed them as an instant error; `sleep` with no operand stays allowed. Every existing D4 verdict-table row keeps its verdict and every existing hookDecision test passes unchanged, the failure-rule cases included.

Finding f-bs-optimize/integration-1e75d554 (bounded): the operand reader is driven with operands near the parser's 65536-character command cap (hookDecision.ts MAX_COMMAND_LENGTH, which makes a longer command no diet match before any operand is read): `sleep ` plus a 65000-character operand of each shape — all digits (a number, deny), digits then `x` (unreadable, deny as unknown), `1` then 64999 `e` characters, and `0x` then 64998 `p` characters — each gets its verdict (the assertion is on the verdict, so the length cap cannot satisfy it) in under 200 ms, and a 1 MB command still gets no diet deny (failure rule, unchanged).

Gate, run from the worktree root on the task's own tree and each output read to its end: `pnpm run test` (the full root suite, never a scoped vitest run), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm biome check .`, `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs --check`. The role templates the harness loads predate the heavy-run fix, so the full suite runs as the wave brief directs (epic spec, "Pre-code review (v6 draft) — changes", item 6): a background task under the heavy lock writing a fresh output file outside the worktree whose last line is `EXIT=<n>` on a line of its own, waited for in foreground calls that each end inside the Bash tool's timeout and use no `sleep`; the result quotes that file's final summary lines and its `EXIT=0`. All five green before hand-back.

functional_clauses: An operand is read as strtod reads one: optional leading `+`; a decimal mantissa, which is digits with an optional `.` and optional further digits (`5`, `5.`, `5.25`) or a `.` followed by digits (`.5`), then an optional exponent (`e`/`E`, optional sign, at least one digit); or `0x`/`0X` hex digits with an optional fraction and an optional binary exponent (`p`/`P`); or `inf`/`infinity` in any case (unbounded). Then at most one unit suffix `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`, and nothing after it. Reading is greedy, so a hex digit is never taken as a suffix. A lone `.` is not a number. Every operand the current reader reads (`2`, `2.`, `.5`, `1.9`, with suffixes) keeps its value.

An operand the reader cannot read is unknown length and counts as 2 s or more (deny), extending epic D4's rule for variables, substitutions and `infinity`; `sleep` with no operand still blocks nothing and is allowed.

The deny reason keeps its format (Blocked: foreground `sleep` of N s, or of unknown length, with the fix). `dietDecision`, `decideHookPayload` and `findForegroundSleeps` keep their signatures (`keeps_exports`).
